name: Under resource limits
desc: Restricted performance families from Matching Arrays, MOVE, REP, ALL, and ROUND. Every case must finish with its listed ordinary outcome under a practical budget sufficient for its explicit input and output. Matching cases return true only after the complete match succeeds. No case permits RESOURCE_LIMIT. Related sizes support scaling measurements, but finite fixtures alone do not establish asymptotic bounds. Expectations also apply under full local validation.

tests.name: Positioned sequence chains
tests.desc: Spec: Matching Arrays. Literal indices and literal string operands satisfy the restricted NEAR performance rule. Exact, displaced, and unsuccessful cases distinguish correctness from merely finding each operand somewhere.

tests.name: 10 sequences, exact indices
tests.desc: 10 two-string sequences each occur exactly once. All are mutually compatible; every preferred index is exact (linear-time case). Matching is the measured operation; the final COPY returns a small success marker.

tests.name: 10 sequences, two elements later
tests.desc: 10 two-string sequences each occur exactly once. All are mutually compatible; actual positions differ from preferred indices by two (polynomial-time case). Matching is the measured operation; the final COPY returns a small success marker.

tests.name: 10 sequences, two elements earlier
tests.desc: 10 two-string sequences each occur exactly once. All are mutually compatible; actual positions differ from preferred indices by two (polynomial-time case). Matching is the measured operation; the final COPY returns a small success marker.

tests.name: 100 sequences, exact negative indices
tests.desc: Negative literal indices resolve to the unique, compatible match positions. This is also an exact-position linear-time case.

tests.name: 10 unique sequences in incompatible order
tests.desc: Every literal occurs exactly once, but their order prevents the complete chain from matching. Uniqueness does not permit accepting individually successful but incompatible matches.

tests.name: 100 unique sequences in incompatible order
tests.desc: Every literal occurs exactly once, but their order prevents the complete chain from matching. Uniqueness does not permit accepting individually successful but incompatible matches.

tests.name: Bulk array moves
tests.desc: Spec: MOVE. Each case is a single action on a flat scalar array with literal indices. Required work is O(array length + number of pairs); input and expected output are explicit.

tests.name: Reverse 32 elements
tests.desc: One MOVE queues all removals and half-index insertions. Indices retain their original meaning until finalization; a single rebuild yields the reversed array.

tests.name: Delete alternating elements from 32
tests.desc: Delete every original even index in one MOVE. Pending deletions must not shift the source indices of later pairs.

tests.name: Queue 31 insertions at one half-index
tests.desc: Move original elements 1 through the end before element 0. Insertions at the same half-index retain assignment order; repeatedly copying the queue or whole array is unnecessary.

tests.desc: One MOVE queues all removals and half-index insertions. Indices retain their original meaning until finalization; a single rebuild yields the reversed array.

tests.name: Repetition bounds and zero-width successors
tests.desc: Spec: REP. Large counts, empty operands, and wildcard searches must remain finite and avoid unnecessary expansion. All operands are literal and structurally valid.

tests.name: Default operand requires 1000 elements
tests.desc: The input has only ten elements. Reject from the length bound without expanding the repetition count or enumerating nonexistent positions.

tests.name: Default operand permits up to 1000 elements
tests.desc: Only eleven successor positions exist. END requires retaining the position after all ten elements, rather than accepting only the first successor.

tests.name: Explicit EXISTS requires 1000 elements
tests.desc: The input has only ten elements. Reject from the length bound without expanding the repetition count or enumerating nonexistent positions.

tests.name: Explicit EXISTS permits up to 1000 elements
tests.desc: Only eleven successor positions exist. END requires retaining the position after all ten elements, rather than accepting only the first successor.

tests.name: 1000 repetitions of an empty sequence
tests.desc: A literal empty SEQ consumes no elements. Its repetition succeeds at the current position without iterating the numeric count.

tests.name: 1000 empty repetitions before a required literal
tests.desc: Repeated empty sequences leave the cursor unchanged; the following literal and END must still execute.

tests.name: Default operand requires 1000000000 elements
tests.desc: The input has only ten elements. Reject from the length bound without expanding the repetition count or enumerating nonexistent positions.

tests.name: Default operand permits up to 1000000000 elements
tests.desc: Only eleven successor positions exist. END requires retaining the position after all ten elements, rather than accepting only the first successor.

tests.name: Explicit EXISTS requires 1000000000 elements
tests.desc: The input has only ten elements. Reject from the length bound without expanding the repetition count or enumerating nonexistent positions.

tests.name: Explicit EXISTS permits up to 1000000000 elements
tests.desc: Only eleven successor positions exist. END requires retaining the position after all ten elements, rather than accepting only the first successor.

tests.name: 1000000000 repetitions of an empty sequence
tests.desc: A literal empty SEQ consumes no elements. Its repetition succeeds at the current position without iterating the numeric count.

tests.name: 1000000000 empty repetitions before a required literal
tests.desc: Repeated empty sequences leave the cursor unchanged; the following literal and END must still execute.

tests.name: Unbounded empty repetition on an empty array
tests.desc: The only reachable cursor is zero; discovering the same cursor again must not cause an infinite loop.

tests.name: Unbounded empty repetition before a literal
tests.desc: Stop enumerating duplicate zero-width successors while preserving the required following match.

tests.name: Unbounded empty repetition does not consume an element
tests.desc: Termination must not be implemented by incorrectly advancing the cursor. END fails while an element remains.

tests.name: Wildcard search with 32 unsuccessful candidates
tests.desc: Every needle is followed by a wildcard span, but the required final string is absent. Default REP must identify successor positions without repeatedly executing EXISTS over every suffix.

tests.name: Wildcard search with 256 unsuccessful candidates
tests.desc: Every needle is followed by a wildcard span, but the required final string is absent. Default REP must identify successor positions without repeatedly executing EXISTS over every suffix.

tests.name: Wildcard search with 2048 unsuccessful candidates
tests.desc: Every needle is followed by a wildcard span, but the required final string is absent. Default REP must identify successor positions without repeatedly executing EXISTS over every suffix.

tests.name: Capture-free intersections
tests.desc: Spec: ALL. These branches contain only simple wildcard repetitions, with no captures or preferences. Sizes increase both branch count and input length; successful and unsuccessful surrounding matches are covered.

tests.name: 4 wildcard branches, final successor required
tests.desc: ALL intersects successor positions. END requires the shared position at the array length; intermediate alternatives are not independent combinations of match histories.

tests.name: 4 wildcard branches, impossible continuation
tests.desc: Every branch admits every cursor position, but no position can satisfy the following literal. Enumerating Cartesian products of equivalent histories is unnecessary.

tests.name: 4 bounded wildcard branches retain their common endpoint
tests.desc: Different lower bounds still have the array length in their intersection. Do not intersect only each branch's first successor.

tests.name: 4 wildcard branches with disjoint bounds
tests.desc: The final exact-length branch has no successor in common with the other branches. Detect an empty intersection without enumerating combinations.

tests.name: 16 wildcard branches, final successor required
tests.desc: ALL intersects successor positions. END requires the shared position at the array length; intermediate alternatives are not independent combinations of match histories.

tests.name: 16 wildcard branches, impossible continuation

tests.name: 16 bounded wildcard branches retain their common endpoint
tests.desc: Different lower bounds still have the array length in their intersection. Do not intersect only each branch's first successor.

tests.name: 16 wildcard branches with disjoint bounds
tests.desc: The final exact-length branch has no successor in common with the other branches. Detect an empty intersection without enumerating combinations.

tests.name: Symbolic decimal exponents
tests.desc: Spec: ROUND. All inputs are strings and all expected outputs are exact strings. Large exponents remain within the portable integer range; only the unnecessary intermediate expansion would be large.

tests.name: Cancel positive exponent 1000
tests.desc: Shift a huge positive exponent back to units. The result is the string 1, not a huge intermediate integer or digit buffer.

tests.name: Cancel negative exponent 1000
tests.desc: Shift a tiny decimal string back to units without converting it to an underflowing host number.

tests.name: Round tiny positive value with exponent -1000
tests.desc: Default HALF_UP rounding to units yields zero. No exponent-sized intermediate string is required.

tests.name: Round tiny positive value upward with exponent -1000
tests.desc: CEILING must retain the fact that the tiny input is positive and nonzero, yielding 1 without host numeric underflow.

tests.name: Round tiny negative value downward with exponent -1000
tests.desc: FLOOR of a tiny negative decimal is -1; symbolic handling must preserve its sign and nonzero magnitude.

tests.name: Keep compact scientific output at exponent 1000
tests.desc: SIG output preserves the original coarse decimal precision. Neither the input nor the result requires an exponent-sized digit buffer.

tests.name: Cancel positive exponent 1000000000
tests.desc: Shift a huge positive exponent back to units. The result is the string 1, not a huge intermediate integer or digit buffer.

tests.name: Cancel negative exponent 1000000000
tests.desc: Shift a tiny decimal string back to units without converting it to an underflowing host number.

tests.name: Round tiny positive value with exponent -1000000000
tests.desc: Default HALF_UP rounding to units yields zero. No exponent-sized intermediate string is required.

tests.name: Round tiny positive value upward with exponent -1000000000
tests.desc: CEILING must retain the fact that the tiny input is positive and nonzero, yielding 1 without host numeric underflow.

tests.name: Round tiny negative value downward with exponent -1000000000
tests.desc: FLOOR of a tiny negative decimal is -1; symbolic handling must preserve its sign and nonzero magnitude.
